author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
People are porting all the software from whatever programming languages to Rust.

But C still runs faster than Rust.   After we ported the software to Rust, which is memory safe, why don't we port it again to C to squeeze out the last 10% of performance gain?

Rust port to C preserves the memory safe, right?

author.name: Benjamin Z.
author.headline: Sr. Engineering Lead at Heitmeyer Consulting

comments.text: Immediately after a port with perfect fidelity? Yes. After that, no.

You’d think that if safety can be automated in this way, why can’t we just apply AI to make the code safe?

Oh yeah that’s right. It would transform the code to a clusterf of nullptr checks.
